title.narrative: EDCTP2: European & Dev. Countries Clinical Trials Partnership 2015 - 2026
EDCTP2: European & Dev. Countries Clinical Trials Partnership 2015 - 2026

description.narrative:
BAKGRUND Partnerskapet mellan Europa och utvecklingsländer inom området klinisk prövning (EDCTP) inrättades 2003 för att hantera den globala hälsokris som orsakas av de tre största fattigdomsrelaterade sjukdomarna hiv/aids, malaria och tuberkulos och för att fullgöra EU:s åtagande att uppnå FN:s millennieutvecklingsmål till 2015. Sverige har genom Sida bidragit med biståndsmedel till EDCTP och Sida har i enlighet med regeringens beslut den 23 oktober 2003 (UD2003/ 53044/ GU) företrätt Sverige inom EDCTP:s första program.
För genomförandet av EDCTP2 har en stiftelse med säte i Haag, Nederländerna, bildats. Medverkande stater ska utse en myndighet/ institution som företrädare och medlem i stiftelsen.
Erfarenheterna av svensk medverkan under partnerskapets första program är mycket goda. Regeringen anser att Sveriges engagemang i EDCTP ska fortsätta under det andra programmet, och har erhållit riksdagens bemyndigande att besluta om deltagande i den stiftelse som inrättats som genomförandestruktur för EDCTP2 (prop. 2014/15:1 utg.omr. 7, bet. 2014/ 15:UU2, rskr. 2014/15:75). Enligt regeringens beslut ska "finansiering av det svenska deltagandet sker genom medel som Sida disponerar inom ramen för utgiftsområde 7, anslag 1:1 Biståndsverksamhet".
Regeringen har beslutat (Regeringsbeslut UF2015/ 12547/UD/USTYR) att Sverige ska delta och har uppdragit åt Sida att företräda Sverige i den stiftelse som bildats som genomförandestruktur (EDCTP2- IS) för det andra programmet för partnerskap mellan Europa och Afrika inom området kliniskprövning (EDCTP2).
Programmet är 10 år, men Sidas beslut handlar enbart om medelstilldelning för kommande femårsperiod av EDCTP2 programmet.
I tillägg till Sidas bidrag ska Sverige räkna in alla offentliga medel som går till forskning inom EDCTP2 fokusområden som del av det totala bidraget. Det inkluderar Sidas bidrag inom globala och bilaterala samarbeten samt Vetenskapsrådets och andra relevanta svenska myndigheters bidrag till forskning inom EDCTP2 fokusområden.
UPPDRAGET EDCTP syftar till att stödja forskningssamarbete som accelererar den kliniska utvecklingen av nya eller förbättrade interventioner för att förebygga eller behandla HIV/AIDS, tuberkulos, malaria och andra försummade infektionssjukdomar i Afrika söder om Sahara.
PROGRAMMET Det andra EDCTP-programmet (EDCTP2) genomförs som en del av det europeiska ramprogrammet för forskning och Innovation, ”Horizon 2020”. Europeiska unionens bidrag till EDCTP kan uppgå till 683 miljoner euro för det 10-åriga programmet (2014-2024), förutsatt att detta motsvaras av bidrag från de deltagande europeiska staterna.
DELTAGANDE De länder som deltar i EDCTP2 som medlemmar i föreningen EDCTP i oktober 2015 är: 14 europeiska länder-Österrike, Danmark, Finland, Frankrike, Tyskland, Irland, Italien, Luxemburg, Nederländerna, Norge, Portugal, Spanien, Sverige, UK; och 14 afrikanska länder – Burkina Faso, Kamerun, Kongo, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Mali, Moçambique, Niger, Senegal, Sydafrika, Tanzania, Uganda och Zambia. Flera länder kan komma att ansluta.
STYRELSEFORMER EDCTP stiftelsen kommer att genomföra EDCTP2-programmet. Stiftelsen styrs av sina medlemmar, de deltagande europeiska och afrikanska staterna, genom generalförsamlingen. Sekretariatet utför verksamheten inom programmet. Det främsta vetenskaplig rådgivande organ till generalförsamlingen och sekretariatet är den rådgivande vetenskaplig kommitté (Scientific Advisory Committee).

Support to European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership to accelerate development of new or improved druugs , vaccines, microbicides and diagnostics against HIV/AIDS; TB and malaria. Support provided since 2004. A new expanded programme is planned within Horizon2020 which will be called EDCTP2.
To accelerate research and development of new or improved diagnostics, drugs, microbicides and vaccines against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and NIDs.

description.narrative:
The EDCTP2 programme is in its completion phase, no new annual work plan or new calls have been published and the EDCTP Secretariat has focused on reviewing periodic and final reports, tracking the progress of projects, collecting outputs, and managing amendment requests.
As previously reported, the EDCTP2 programme was planned to run until the end of 2024, but due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the end of the programme has been extended until the end of 2026 to allow completion of all project grants (no-cost extensions of project duration). Likewise, Sida has extended the end date of the activity period of the agreement with the EDCTP Association until the end of 2026.
Examples of project results
The EDCTP2 programme has adhered to its strategic vision and continues to deliver significant impact on poverty-related diseases and clinical research capacity in sub-Saharan Africa. In the end of 2024, 36 out of 48 projects supported by Sida had reached their end date and were completed.
Research area: Vaccine and neutralising antibody development for disease prevention
Prevention of diarrhoeal disease in children: Enterotoxigenic E. coli bacteria (ETEC) are estimated to cause about 220 million diarrhoea episodes globally, with about 75 million episodes in children under 5 years of age. ETEC is a significant health concern for children, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, because of its high prevalence and potential for severe illness and long-term developmental impacts. Sida is supporting two projects on a vaccine (Etvax) developed by the Swedish biopharma company Scandinavian Biopharma Holding AB against diarrheal disease caused by ETEC. The projects are investigating vaccine efficacy and evaluate the vaccine in phase I, II and III clinical trials in Zambia and The Gambia. Etvax is currently the most advanced ETEC candidate vaccine in clinical development (https://www.who.int/teams/immunization-vaccines-and-biologicals/diseases/enterotoxigenic-escherichia-coli-(etec)) and data from these trials will be critical for seeking licensure and WHO prequalification.
Research area: Drugs for treatment and prevention
Malaria treatment in pregnancy and newborns: The Sida-supported PAMAfrica consortium is conducting clinical trials to evaluate new malaria treatments for Africa. There is currently no evidence-based treatment for the smallest babies (under 5 kg) with malaria. In April 2024, the PAMAfrica consortium announced positive results from their phase II/III CALINA study demonstrating that a new dose regimen of an existing treatment has good efficacy and safety for babies weighing less than 5 kg with malaria. A regulatory dossier was submitted to SwissMedic, and in July 2025, authorisation for the treatment was granted under the Marketing Authorisation for Global Health Products procedure. Approvals in eight African countries are ongoing, thus making this new treatment available to very young, low-weight infants, who currently have no evidence-based treatment options.
Capacity development area: Pharmacovigilance
Pharmacovigilance is the science and activities relating to the detection, assessment, understanding and prevention of adverse effects or any other medicine or vaccine-related problem that may only emerge after clinical trial and treatment authorization processes when procducts are used by a heterogenous population, including people with other concurrent diseases, and over a long period of time.
The Sida-supported PROFORMA project has helped to improve pharmacovigilance infrastructure, post-marketing surveillance system and clinical trial regulatory capacity in Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. The project successfully demonstrated the feasibility of conducting large-scale active safety surveillance in mass drug administration and vaccination programmes through effective collaboration between academia, national medicine regulators, and public health programmes in African settings.
The experience gained during PROFORMAs active safety surveillance of HPV vaccine in Ethiopia helped the Ethiopian authorities to do vaccine surveillance for COVID-19. The project also developed an undergraduate pharmacovigilance curriculum which is now adopted by PROFORMA participating medical universities in East Africa as well as post-graduate programme in pharmacovigilance and pharmaco-epidemiology accredited by the Tanzania Commission for Universities and adopted by Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences in Dar es Salaam.
The project has to date reported the graduation of 12 postgraduate students (6 PhD and 6 MSc) and the publication of 26 manuscripts.
Furthermore, the PROFORMA project delivered a cascade of short courses and workshops in various fields of pharmacovigilance, including risk management, safety monitoring and communication. To date the consortium has trained over 50 000 pharmacovigilance experts from national regulatory authorities and medical university staff through face-to-face, virtual or hybrid learning. PROFORMAs Short Term Training approach has elevated regulatory capacity, offering valuable lessons for protecting public health continent-wide.
A closure symposium for the PROFORMA project was held at Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm in December 2024. The event convened consortium members from 10 institutions across six countries (Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Sweden and the Netherlands) alongside graduates and key stakeholders.
Publications
In the end of 2024, the EDCTP Secretariat recorded 290 scientific publications associated with Sida-funded projects (out of more than 2100 publications from all projects under the EDCTP2 programme). The majority of publications are related to projects in the emerging diseases area (61%), reflecting Sida's substantial investment in this topic, followed by HIV and HIV-associated infections (17%), malaria (9%), tuberculosis (5,5%), diarrhoeal diseases (3%) and neglected infectious diseases (3%).
Publication numbers have grown steadily over the last years and are expected to continue to grow as a number of clinical trials is still ongoing and further results will emerge.
